name: Acyloin Condensation
note: Reductive coupling of two esters by sodium metal gives an α-hydroxy ketone (acyloin); works well for medium and large rings.

name: Aldol Condensation
note: An enolate adds to a carbonyl; dehydration of the β-hydroxy carbonyl gives an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Arndt–Eistert Homologation
note: One-carbon chain extension of a carboxylic acid via an α-diazoketone and a Wolff rearrangement.

name: Baeyer–Villiger Oxidation
note: A peracid inserts an oxygen next to the carbonyl: ketones become esters, cyclic ketones become lactones. The more substituted group migrates.

name: Bamford–Stevens Reaction
note: Weak base decomposes a tosylhydrazone via a diazo compound / carbene (or cation), giving the MORE substituted alkene (compare Shapiro).

name: Baylis–Hillman Reaction
note: A tertiary amine (or phosphine) catalyst couples the α-position of an activated alkene to an aldehyde, giving a densely functionalized allylic alcohol.

name: Beckmann Rearrangement
note: Acid converts an oxime into an amide; the group anti to the leaving OH migrates (cyclohexanone oxime → ε-caprolactam, Nylon-6).

name: Benzidine Rearrangement
note: Acid-catalyzed [5,5]-sigmatropic rearrangement of hydrazobenzene to 4,4'-diaminobiphenyl (benzidine).

name: Michaelis–Arbuzov Reaction
note: A trialkyl phosphite attacks an alkyl halide (SN2); halide then dealkylates the phosphonium salt to give a phosphonate.

name: Benzilic Acid Rearrangement
note: Hydroxide adds to a 1,2-diketone and an aryl group undergoes 1,2-shift, giving an α-hydroxy carboxylic acid.

name: Birch Reduction
note: Dissolving-metal reduction of arenes to non-conjugated 1,4-cyclohexadienes; donor groups (OMe) end up on a remaining alkene carbon.

name: Blanc Chloromethylation
note: Electrophilic aromatic substitution that installs a CH2Cl group using formaldehyde and HCl with a Lewis acid.

name: Bucherer Reaction
note: Reversible conversion of naphthols into naphthylamines with ammonia and bisulfite (via a tetralone sulfonate).

name: Cannizzaro Reaction
note: Non-enolizable aldehydes disproportionate in strong base by hydride transfer: one becomes the alcohol, the other the carboxylic acid.

name: Claisen Condensation
note: An ester enolate attacks a second ester molecule giving a β-keto ester (driven by deprotonation of the product).

name: Claisen Rearrangement
note: [3,3]-Sigmatropic rearrangement of allyl vinyl / allyl aryl ethers to γ,δ-unsaturated carbonyls or o-allyl phenols.

name: Clemmensen Reduction
note: Reduces aldehydes/ketones (especially aryl ketones) to CH2 under strongly ACIDIC conditions.

name: Cope Rearrangement
note: [3,3]-Sigmatropic shift of a 1,5-diene to an isomeric 1,5-diene through a chair-like transition state.

name: Corey–Winter Olefination
note: Stereospecific conversion of 1,2-diols (as cyclic thiocarbonates) into alkenes with a trialkyl phosphite.

name: Curtius Rearrangement
note: An acyl azide loses N2 and R migrates (with retention) to give an isocyanate, which can be trapped to amines, carbamates or ureas.

name: Darzens Condensation
note: An α-halo ester enolate adds to a carbonyl and the alkoxide closes onto the C–Cl to give an α,β-epoxy (glycidic) ester.

name: Chichibabin Reaction
note: Nucleophilic amination of pyridine at C-2 by sodium amide, with formal loss of hydride.

name: Strecker Synthesis
note: Aldehyde + ammonia + cyanide give an α-aminonitrile; hydrolysis gives the α-amino acid.

name: Swern Oxidation
note: DMSO activated by oxalyl chloride oxidizes 1° alcohols to aldehydes (no over-oxidation) and 2° alcohols to ketones; Me2S is the smelly by-product.

name: Vilsmeier–Haack Reaction
note: Formylation of electron-rich arenes by the chloroiminium ion (Vilsmeier reagent) generated from DMF and POCl3.

name: Hantzsch Thiazole Synthesis
note: An α-haloketone condenses with a thioamide (S-alkylation, then cyclodehydration) to form a thiazole.

name: Hantzsch Pyridine Synthesis
note: Two β-keto esters, an aldehyde and ammonia assemble a 1,4-dihydropyridine; oxidation gives the pyridine.

name: Wittig Reaction
note: A phosphonium ylide converts an aldehyde/ketone into an alkene via an oxaphosphetane; Ph3P=O is the by-product.

name: Stork Enamine Alkylation
note: Enamines are neutral enolate equivalents: Michael addition or alkylation, then hydrolysis, gives the α-substituted ketone.

name: Diazotization
note: Primary aryl amines react with nitrous acid (NaNO2/HCl) at low temperature to give arenediazonium salts.

name: Williamson Ether Synthesis
note: SN2 reaction of an alkoxide or phenoxide with a primary alkyl halide gives an ether.

name: Schmidt Reaction
note: Hydrazoic acid and strong acid convert ketones into amides (and carboxylic acids into amines) with loss of N2.

name: Wolff–Kishner Reduction
note: Hydrazone formation, then strong base and heat, reduces C=O to CH2 with loss of N2: the BASIC counterpart of the Clemmensen.

name: Ozonolysis
note: Ozone cleaves C=C bonds via molozonide/ozonide; reductive work-up (Me2S, Zn) gives aldehydes and ketones.

name: Mannich Reaction
note: An enolizable carbonyl adds to an iminium ion (from formaldehyde + amine) to give a β-amino carbonyl (Mannich base).

name: Michael Addition
note: 1,4-(Conjugate) addition of a stabilized carbanion to an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Robinson Annulation
note: Michael addition to methyl vinyl ketone followed by intramolecular aldol condensation builds a new cyclohexenone ring.

name: Pinacol Rearrangement
note: Acid converts a 1,2-diol into a ketone via a carbocation and a 1,2-alkyl shift (pinacol → pinacolone).

name: Diels–Alder Reaction
note: Concerted [4+2] cycloaddition of a diene and a dienophile giving a cyclohexene; suprafacial and stereospecific.

name: Prins Reaction
note: Electrophilic addition of a protonated aldehyde to an alkene; in water the cation is trapped to give a 1,3-diol.

name: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky Reaction
note: α-Bromination of carboxylic acids through the enol of the intermediate acyl bromide.

name: Haloform Reaction
note: Methyl ketones are exhaustively halogenated and cleaved by base into a carboxylate and a haloform (CHI3 = yellow precipitate).

name: Fischer Indole Synthesis
note: An aryl hydrazone undergoes acid-catalyzed [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement and loses NH3 to form an indole.

name: Knoevenagel Condensation
note: Condensation of an aldehyde with an active-methylene compound using a weak amine base, giving an alkylidene product.

name: Grignard Reaction
note: Organomagnesium halides add to carbonyl groups; ketones give tertiary alcohols, aldehydes secondary alcohols.

name: Friedel–Crafts Acylation
note: An acylium ion (acyl chloride + AlCl3) acylates an arene; no rearrangement and no poly-acylation.

name: Friedel–Crafts Alkylation
note: A carbocation from an alkyl halide + Lewis acid alkylates an arene (prone to rearrangement and polyalkylation).

name: Gattermann–Koch Reaction
note: Formylation of simple arenes with CO/HCl under Lewis-acid catalysis, via the formyl cation.

name: Reimer–Tiemann Reaction
note: ortho-Formylation of phenols via dichlorocarbene generated from chloroform and hydroxide.

name: Kolbe–Schmitt Reaction
note: Sodium phenoxide is carboxylated by CO2 under pressure to give salicylic acid.

name: Sandmeyer Reaction
note: Copper(I) salts (CuCl, CuBr, CuCN) replace the N2+ group of an arenediazonium salt.

name: Balz–Schiemann Reaction
note: Thermal decomposition of an arenediazonium tetrafluoroborate gives an aryl fluoride.

name: Gabriel Synthesis
note: N-Alkylation of potassium phthalimide followed by hydrazinolysis gives a primary amine free of over-alkylation.

name: Hofmann Rearrangement
note: A primary amide loses one carbon (as CO2) to give an amine, via an N-bromoamide and an isocyanate.

name: Hofmann Elimination
note: E2 elimination of a quaternary ammonium hydroxide gives the LESS substituted (Hofmann) alkene.

name: Cope Elimination
note: A tertiary amine N-oxide undergoes concerted syn (Ei) elimination on heating, giving an alkene and a hydroxylamine.

name: Mitsunobu Reaction
note: PPh3/DEAD activate an alcohol so an acidic nucleophile displaces it by SN2, with INVERSION of configuration.

name: Appel Reaction
note: Converts alcohols into alkyl halides under mild, neutral conditions; Ph3P=O is the driving force.

name: Dess–Martin Oxidation
note: The hypervalent iodine reagent Dess–Martin periodinane mildly oxidizes alcohols to aldehydes or ketones at rt.

name: Jones Oxidation
note: Chromic acid in acetone oxidizes 1° alcohols all the way to carboxylic acids and 2° alcohols to ketones.

name: Oppenauer Oxidation
note: Aluminium-alkoxide-mediated hydride transfer from an alcohol to acetone; the reverse of the MPV reduction.

name: Meerwein–Ponndorf–Verley Reduction
note: Chemoselective reduction of aldehydes/ketones by hydride transfer from isopropanol through a six-membered Al transition state.

name: Wagner–Meerwein Rearrangement
note: A 1,2-alkyl (or hydride) shift converts a carbocation into a more stable one, followed by elimination or capture.

name: Favorskii Rearrangement
note: α-Halo ketones rearrange in base through a cyclopropanone to carboxylic acid derivatives; cyclic ones ring-contract.

name: Wolff Rearrangement
note: An α-diazoketone loses N2 and undergoes 1,2-shift to a ketene, which MeOH traps as the homologated ester.

name: Fries Rearrangement
note: Lewis acids convert aryl esters into ortho- and para-hydroxyaryl ketones.

name: Dakin Oxidation
note: ortho/para-Hydroxy aryl aldehydes are converted to phenols (via an aryl formate) by basic hydrogen peroxide.

name: Wacker Oxidation
note: Pd(II)-catalyzed Markovnikov oxidation of terminal alkenes to methyl ketones; Cu/O2 re-oxidize the palladium.

name: Sharpless Asymmetric Epoxidation
note: Ti/tartrate-catalyzed enantioselective epoxidation of ALLYLIC ALCOHOLS; the tartrate enantiomer selects the alkene face.

name: Upjohn Dihydroxylation
note: Catalytic OsO4 with NMO as the stoichiometric re-oxidant converts alkenes into cis-1,2-diols.

name: Simmons–Smith Reaction
note: A zinc carbenoid (ICH2ZnI) adds stereospecifically to alkenes to form cyclopropanes.

name: Brown Hydroboration–Oxidation
note: Syn, anti-Markovnikov addition of H–B followed by oxidation with retention gives the less substituted alcohol.

name: Heck Reaction
note: Pd-catalyzed coupling of an aryl/vinyl halide with an alkene giving the substituted, usually E, alkene.

name: Suzuki Coupling
note: Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling of an organoboron compound with an aryl/vinyl halide; requires a base.

name: Stille Coupling
note: Pd-catalyzed coupling of organostannanes with organic halides; tolerates almost any functional group (but tin is toxic).

name: Sonogashira Coupling
note: Pd/Cu co-catalyzed coupling of terminal alkynes with aryl or vinyl halides.

name: Negishi Coupling
note: Pd- or Ni-catalyzed coupling of organozinc reagents with organic halides.

name: Kumada Coupling
note: Ni- or Pd-catalyzed coupling of Grignard reagents with aryl/vinyl halides.

name: Buchwald–Hartwig Amination
note: Pd-catalyzed C–N bond formation between aryl halides and amines.

name: Ullmann Coupling
note: Copper-mediated homocoupling of aryl halides to symmetrical biaryls.

name: Glaser Coupling
note: Oxidative copper-catalyzed homocoupling of terminal alkynes to 1,3-diynes.

name: Ring-Closing Metathesis
note: Ru-carbene catalysts exchange alkene partners; intramolecular metathesis closes a ring and releases ethylene.

name: Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons Reaction
note: Phosphonate carbanions olefinate aldehydes, mainly giving E-alkenes plus a water-soluble phosphate by-product.

name: Peterson Olefination
note: α-Silyl carbanions add to carbonyls; the β-hydroxysilane then eliminates (syn with base, anti with acid) to an alkene.

name: McMurry Reaction
note: Low-valent titanium reductively couples two carbonyl groups into an alkene.

name: Pinacol Coupling
note: One-electron reduction of carbonyls gives ketyl radicals that dimerize to 1,2-diols.

name: Reformatsky Reaction
note: A zinc enolate formed from an α-halo ester adds to aldehydes or ketones giving β-hydroxy esters.

name: Henry Reaction
note: Base-catalyzed nitro-aldol: a nitronate adds to an aldehyde to give a β-nitro alcohol.

name: Perkin Reaction
note: Aromatic aldehydes condense with an acid anhydride (carboxylate as base) to give cinnamic acids.

name: Dieckmann Condensation
note: Intramolecular Claisen condensation of a diester to a cyclic β-keto ester (best for 5- and 6-membered rings).

name: Benzoin Condensation
note: Cyanide (or an NHC) catalyzes umpolung dimerization of aromatic aldehydes to α-hydroxy ketones.

name: Wurtz Reaction
note: Sodium metal couples two alkyl halides into a symmetrical alkane.

name: Corey–Chaykovsky Reaction
note: A sulfur ylide adds to a carbonyl and displaces the sulfide intramolecularly to form an epoxide.

name: Corey–Fuchs Reaction
note: Aldehyde → 1,1-dibromoalkene (Wittig-type) → terminal alkyne by double lithiation: a one-carbon homologation.

name: Seyferth–Gilbert Homologation
note: A diazomethylphosphonate (here the Ohira–Bestmann reagent) converts aldehydes into terminal alkynes.

name: Nef Reaction
note: Acid hydrolysis of a nitronate salt converts a primary or secondary nitroalkane into an aldehyde or ketone.

name: Hunsdiecker Reaction
note: Silver carboxylates react with bromine to give alkyl bromides with loss of CO2 (radical chain).

name: Wohl–Ziegler Bromination
note: Allylic or benzylic bromination with NBS under radical conditions (low Br2 concentration).

name: Anionic Oxy-Cope Rearrangement
note: [3,3]-Shift of a 1,5-dien-3-olate, accelerated ~10^10-fold by the alkoxide, giving a δ,ε-unsaturated carbonyl.

name: Paal–Knorr Pyrrole Synthesis
note: 1,4-Diketones condense with primary amines or NH3 to give pyrroles (with acid alone: furans).

name: Skraup Quinoline Synthesis
note: Aniline + glycerol (dehydrated to acrolein) with acid and an oxidant gives quinoline.

name: Bischler–Napieralski Reaction
note: Cyclodehydration of β-arylethylamides to 3,4-dihydroisoquinolines.

name: Pictet–Spengler Reaction
note: A β-arylethylamine condenses with an aldehyde and the iminium ion cyclizes onto the arene (tetrahydroisoquinolines / β-carbolines).

name: Biginelli Reaction
note: Three-component condensation of urea, a β-keto ester and an aldehyde to a 3,4-dihydropyrimidin-2-one.

name: Azide–Alkyne Huisgen Cycloaddition
note: Cu(I)-catalyzed 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of an azide and a terminal alkyne gives a 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazole ("click").

name: Paternò–Büchi Reaction
note: Photochemical [2+2] cycloaddition of an excited carbonyl with an alkene gives an oxetane.

name: Nazarov Cyclization
note: Acid-promoted 4π conrotatory electrocyclization of a divinyl ketone gives a cyclopentenone.

name: Pauson–Khand Reaction
note: Cobalt-mediated [2+2+1] cycloaddition of an alkyne, an alkene and CO to a cyclopentenone.

name: Mukaiyama Aldol Reaction
note: Lewis-acid-mediated addition of a silyl enol ether to an aldehyde: an aldol without a strong base.

name: Corey–Bakshi–Shibata Reduction
note: An oxazaborolidine catalyst directs borane reduction of ketones to enantioenriched secondary alcohols.

name: Noyori Asymmetric Hydrogenation
note: Ru–BINAP catalysts hydrogenate β-keto esters (and functionalized alkenes) with very high enantioselectivity.

name: Luche Reduction
note: CeCl3-modified NaBH4 performs selective 1,2-reduction of enones to allylic alcohols.

name: Rosenmund Reduction
note: Hydrogenation of acyl chlorides over a poisoned Pd catalyst stops at the aldehyde.

name: Lindlar Hydrogenation
note: A poisoned Pd catalyst semi-hydrogenates alkynes to cis (Z) alkenes.

name: Staudinger Reduction
note: A phosphine attacks an azide to form an iminophosphorane (−N2); hydrolysis gives the amine and Ph3P=O.

name: Eschweiler–Clarke Methylation
note: Exhaustive N-methylation of amines with formaldehyde and formic acid (hydride donor) that stops at the tertiary amine.

name: Ritter Reaction
note: A carbocation is trapped by a nitrile; hydrolysis of the nitrilium ion gives an N-alkyl amide.

name: Fischer Esterification
note: Acid-catalyzed equilibrium condensation of a carboxylic acid and an alcohol to an ester (drive by excess alcohol or removing water).

name: Steglich Esterification
note: Carbodiimide activation with DMAP catalysis esterifies even hindered alcohols under mild, neutral conditions.

name: Krapcho Decarboxylation
note: Halide attacks the ester alkyl group of a malonate or β-keto ester, then CO2 is lost: one ester removed under near-neutral conditions.

name: Malonic Ester Synthesis
note: Alkylation of diethyl malonate, then hydrolysis and decarboxylation, gives a substituted acetic acid.

name: Acetoacetic Ester Synthesis
note: Alkylation of ethyl acetoacetate, then hydrolysis and decarboxylation, gives a substituted methyl ketone.

name: Barton–McCombie Deoxygenation
note: Radical deoxygenation of alcohols through a thiocarbonyl derivative (xanthate) using tin hydride.

name: Shapiro Reaction
note: A tosylhydrazone + 2 equiv RLi gives a vinyllithium; protonation gives the LESS substituted alkene (compare Bamford–Stevens).

name: Bouveault–Blanc Reduction
note: Sodium in ethanol reduces esters to primary alcohols (the pre-LiAlH4 method; compare the acyloin condensation in aprotic solvent).

name: Willgerodt–Kindler Reaction
note: Aryl alkyl ketones are converted into terminal thioamides with sulfur and a secondary amine (carbonyl 'walks' to the chain end).

name: Ugi Reaction
note: Four-component coupling of an aldehyde, an amine, a carboxylic acid and an isocyanide to an α-acylamino amide.

name: Passerini Reaction
note: Three-component coupling of a carbonyl compound, a carboxylic acid and an isocyanide to an α-acyloxy amide (no amine, unlike Ugi).

name: Chugaev Elimination
note: Pyrolytic syn (Ei) elimination of a xanthate ester giving an alkene, COS and MeSH.

name: Pinnick Oxidation
note: Chlorite oxidizes aldehydes (even α,β-unsaturated ones) to carboxylic acids; the alkene scavenges HOCl.

name: Lemieux–Johnson Oxidation
note: OsO4 dihydroxylation then periodate cleavage converts an alkene into two carbonyls: an ozonolysis alternative.

name: Prilezhaev Epoxidation
note: A peracid transfers an oxygen atom to an alkene in a concerted, stereospecific syn addition to give an epoxide.

name: Tiffeneau–Demjanov Rearrangement
note: Diazotization of a 1-aminomethyl-cycloalkanol triggers ring expansion to the one-carbon-larger cycloalkanone.

name: Hosomi–Sakurai Reaction
note: Lewis-acid-promoted allylation of carbonyls with allylsilanes (β-silyl cation stabilization).

name: Tsuji–Trost Reaction
note: Pd(0) ionizes allylic leaving groups to π-allyl complexes, which are attacked by soft nucleophiles.

name: Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation
note: OsO4 with a cinchona-alkaloid ligand (AD-mix) gives enantioenriched syn-1,2-diols; α and β mixes give opposite enantiomers.
